subject: humanities
passage: Musicologist Ilse Kaarna wanted to know the pitch at which music was performed in a north German town around 1700. The town's church organ, built in 1698, survives and today sounds close to modern standard pitch. Later organ builders who raised an instrument's pitch to keep up with changing fashions usually did so by trimming its pipes, since a shorter pipe sounds higher; lowering a pipe's pitch requires adding metal to lengthen it. Kaarna found that most of the organ's pipes bear trim marks made with tools first used in the mid-1800s, but she found no sign that metal had ever been added. Based on this evidence, Kaarna can most reasonably conclude that the organ ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: was the only organ in the region to have its pitch changed after 1700.
choices.B: sounded higher around 1700 than it does today.
choices.C: can reveal nothing about the pitch that musicians used around 1700.
choices.D: probably sounded lower around 1700 than it does today.

explanation.why: Trimming a pipe raises its pitch, and the trim marks were made long after the organ was built. No metal was added, so nothing was done that would have lowered the pitch. The organ's pitch was therefore raised at some point, which means it was probably lower in 1700 than it is now.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text discusses only this one organ and says nothing about other organs in the region.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This reverses the evidence: the later trimming raised the pitch, so the organ was most likely lower in 1700, not higher.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The evidence does tell Kaarna something: the direction of the change suggests the pitch around 1700 was lower than today's.
explanation.D: Correct. Later trimming raised the pipes' pitch and nothing lowered it, so the organ most likely sounded lower when it was new.
